summary.answer: Creates an8-item spray/gesture wheel with controller prompt/pointer. Visible requires held input and excludes game-ended, remote control, vehicle, demo, death, killcam, scoreboard, spectating, prematch and laststand conditions. State changes lock/unlock stick with0/125 delay and disable wheel selection when hidden. Right-stick callbacks act only while visible; the exact quick-spray input enum triggers registration. PC confirm resets state; selected helper registrations do not prove a spray/gesture actually executes.

summary.answer: Creates a10-item CalloutWheel, prompt/pointer and focus proxy. The exact recovered Visible predicate98–116 has no truthy normal return. If the initial IsCalloutsButtonPressed result is false/nil,115 returns that result. With a truthy initial result, a falsy EnableCalloutWheel result can return early at110; every other normally returning path through that initial truthy branch reaches the unconditional f7_local0=false at113 before115. Even when all five visibility exclusions and prematch/theater/laststand gates permit the inner assignment105 to compute true,113 overwrites it with false. Numeric0 is truthy and does not create another truthy return path. Helper/table/enum/provider errors may prevent any return; missing values do not establish feasibility of this predicate returning true. This is a preserved recovered-source control-flow limit, not a repair of the dump or proof of original game behavior. The registered setState callback, if delivered and its separate IsSelfInState(self,"Visible") test is truthy, requests MenuDelayedSetRightStickLock(menu,delivered controller,0,true); otherwise it requests that helper with125,false and then DisableWheelSelection. Those are requests, not established helper effects or timing. Length/degrees callbacks request selection changes only under their shown Visible guard; PC confirm requests a state reset. The callout and mouse-drag helper requests do not establish actual callback delivery, successful input locking, a server-visible callout event or native/VM/build/runtime behavior.
